name: SpaceX Starmind AI1 orbital data center satellite
note: Parity model for the v1.1 'SpaceX AI Satellites' type (Starmind AI1, a million-satellite dawn-dusk disk). Body frame: +Z to the Sun, +X toward nadir, +Y along the span. A flat 10 x 3 x 0.6 m bus (it stacks PEZ-style); two wings of three 3.2 m strips spanning 70 m, on trusses across a 3.5 m gap; two white radiators standing edge-on to the Sun from the bus's flat faces, 10 m long and 20 m top to bottom. 10 lobes: a million satellites fly it. Trusses, spars, fittings and terminals are render-only detail.

sources.subject: attitude
sources.value: Sun-pointing (+Z to the Sun), +X toward nadir; arrays tilted off the Sun by the flare-mitigation slider
sources.source: Starmind AI1 as specified by the project owner (2026-09-24, from the AI1 spec sheet image): 'two large sun pointing panels with a wingspan of 70m', 'edge on radiators on the top and bottom of the bus with a deployed height of 20m'; the bus 'flatter, proportions similar to a door ... as wide as the solar panels', 'the radiators need to be the same length as that body', panels and radiators extending 'horizontally (panels) and vertically (radiators)' with 'widths contained within the length of the bus', 'flat, so it can pancake on top of other datacenters' (PEZ-style stacking), and 'the larger gap between the panels and the satellite body ... with large trusses'. AI1 spec sheet: 150 kW solar array at 250 W/m2, 110 m2 deployable liquid radiator, 150 kW peak compute. The tilt joint is the v1.1 legacy type's (SunTrackingTilted), kept for the slider.
